text:
jane: Quick brain-dump: what if we introduce a tiny per-shard sidecar (shard-###.aux) that contains a light-weight manifest: short fingerprint, relative layer offsets, quantization tag, abi version and an optional signature. runtime does a single small GET to decide hotstart strategy before touching big blob.

mike: Sounds promising. main benefits I see: avoid a full mmap/parse just to learn if shard is compatible; faster failure on mismatch; and we can pick indexing vs stream path proactively. questions: how do we place the aux across packaging formats (raw shards, tar/gzip bundles, object storage metadata)?

jane: plan for placement: 1) sidecar file next to shard (s3/object) 2) included inside model bundle as shard-000.aux (preferably stored uncompressed) 3) as object metadata when publishers prefer metadata entries. loader searches in that order.

carla: tradeoffs: a) atomicity - need a clear publish commit flow so aux and shard don't drift. b) compatibility - old loaders should ignore aux silently. c) extra files to track in registries.

mike: for atomicity we can write shard payload first, then aux last, and finally a tiny commit marker (shard-000.aux.commit). commit file acts as the ready flag and contains version and signature. loaders treat aux as authoritative only if commit exists.

drew: what about leases / dedupe: when many nodes try to warm the same shard, we should avoid duplicate heavy downloads. I propose keeping ephemeral leases in our runtime metadata store (etcd/consul). aux only carries a stable boot id and fingerprint; runtime uses metadata store to negotiate hotstart ownership. we avoid object-store writes on lease transitions.

jane: agree. aux remains read-only artifact in object storage. runtime lease is ephemeral and kept off-object-store. this keeps publish cheap and keeps aux trustworthy for first-read heuristics.

carla: another corner: mmap offsets. if aux stores absolute file offsets, repacking or embedding in bundles will break them. store relative offsets: offset from start-of-array within the shard plus a small abi field that explains packing expectations. loader can compute absolute if it mmap's from known base.

mike: signature idea: include a short sha256 fingerprint and signer id. signed aux allows runtime to trust the fingerprint without fetching the whole shard. add quant_tag to help warmup choose fp16/q8h optimized kernels ahead of time.

drew: implementation sketch as plain text example (aux schema is a single line JSON blob):
shard-000.aux -> {"abi":"1","layers":[{"name":"mlp.fc1","offset":128,"len":65536}],"fingerprint":"sha256:abc...","quant_tag":"q8h","signed_by":"release-v3"}
shard-000.aux.commit -> {"ready":true,"ts":1805556789}  <-- tiny commit marker

jane: rollout steps: 1) loader accepts aux if present, falls back silently when missing. 2) runtime uses aux only to choose warmup strategy and prefetch hints. 3) publishing toolchain produces aux and a commit marker when publishing bundles. 4) registry/CI validates commit presence as optional gate for signed releases.

carla: ops concerns: relying on signed metadata means release infra needs key management and signing roles. ops-bot: creating infra ticket infra/2026 to update registry and signing perms.

ops-bot: noted infra/2026 created. tag: release-signer.

mike: one more: for gzipped bundles we should prefer storing aux uncompressed alongside the compressed shard to avoid needing partial decompression. if embedded, prefer a separate entry in the tarball header and mark it with a known mime/type.

drew: runtime heuristics: if aux indicates large contiguous layers we prefer mmap if base format supports it; if many small scattered arrays we prefer streaming + async prefetch. aux can carry a simple heuristic flag ("prefetch_hint": "mmap|stream").

jane: and include an "abi" per-shard so loaders can fast-fail when aux schema doesn't match. per-shard abi lets different shards of same model evolve independently if needed.

carla: testing checklist: publish test bundles with and without aux, ensure loader fallback path exercised, validate commit marker semantics, exercise lease path in metadata store under high-concurrency warmstart (stress test).

mike: doc/CI: add a small linter that checks for shard-*.aux and shard-*.aux.commit in release bundles when signing is enabled. optional for unsigned test releases.

jane: i'll draft a short RFC follow-up with schema, file locations, commit semantics, and runtime lease integration notes. thanks all. :thumbsup:
